rv.q: Not a syllable of which, I'm happy to report, isn't uproarious.
Mark Rylance ("Boeing-Boeing") appears wearing a pair of terrible false teeth and delivers an astonishing, 20-minute soliloquy that leaves audiences in hysterics, stunned and cheering.

At the top of David Hirson's faux-Moliere souffle, “La Bete,” the astoundingly intense actor Mark Rylance flawlessly delivers a monologue — a rhyming, tour de force, just-can't-stop logorrhea — that occupies something like 400 lines of script on the page and takes at least a half-hour to deliver on a Broadway stage.

The revival that opened last night is as good as can be, zippily directed by Matthew Warchus ("The Norman Conquests") and powered by a dream cast led by David Hyde Pierce, Joanna Lumley and Mark Rylance.

Mark Rylance dazzled audiences with his high-octane physicality in the recent Broadway revival of Boeing-Boeing, and the Tony Award-winning actor proves to be equally astonishing in Matthew Warchus' often hilarious revival of David Hirson's 1991 rhyming-verse play, La Bete, now at the Music Box.
His performance is a masterclass in comic pomposity.
Although there’s no intermission, this is a show in which you wouldn’t miss much by walking out after the first half-hour.
Four stars (****) for this unmissable jewel.
For all his rock-star strutting, he shows us the commoner who became a statesman while grappling with personal and national crises.
David Hirson's 'La Bête' is a theatrical anomaly—a rhyming comedy that manages to be both pretentious and genuinely funny, often at the same time.

cn.t: Critics praise Mark Rylance's virtuosic 30-minute opening monologue in this rhyming-couplet farce, though many find the play itself an uneven intellectual exercise that doesn't sustain its initial brilliance.

vs.sum: The Music Box Theatre offers excellent sightlines from most seats, making it ideal for intimate dramas, though sound quality can vary. The theater's charming Georgian-inspired design adds to its ambiance, while comfort and facilities are average for a Broadway venue.

acc.note: 5 wheelchair spaces in Orchestra. No steps from sidewalk. Infrared devices available.
